source_title: Business Formation Statistics (U.S. Census Bureau) - record annual business applications in 2023
publisher_issuer: U.S. Census Bureau (Business Formation Statistics program)
company_context: Population-level dataset, not a single company. Census Business Formation Statistics (BFS) tracks business applications (measured by applications for an Employer Identification Number) and actual and projected employer business formations (measured by first payroll-tax liability), at monthly and annual frequency.
business_type: All new U.S. business applications and formations (cross-sectoral)
company_size_stage: Business formation / startup stage (whole-population entry flow)
geography: United States (national, with state and county detail)
macro_context: Post-pandemic surge in U.S. business formation sustained through 2023 despite rising interest rates and inflation; third consecutive record-setting year for applications.
outcome_category: 12 - stable / healthy base rate (record formation flow, population entry statistics)
evidence_summary: A record 5.5 million new business applications were filed in the United States in 2023, the highest annual total on record and the third consecutive year above 5 million, following about 5.3 million in 2022 and about 5.4 million in 2021. Monthly seasonally adjusted application counts in 2023 ran in the mid-400-thousands range (for example, about 464,838 in November 2023 and about 472,961 in September 2023). BFS also distinguishes high-propensity applications (those more likely to become employer businesses) and projects actual employer formations from first payroll-tax liability. These are population entry-flow base rates that characterize the health of U.S. business formation, appropriate for stable-healthy base-rate calibration; they do not by themselves indicate firm-level distress.

source_backed_metrics.application_proxy: applications for an Employer Identification Number (EIN)
source_backed_metrics.formation_proxy: actual and projected employer formations from first payroll-tax liability

owner_decision_context: Not applicable at firm level; the dataset reflects aggregate entry decisions by U.S. founders.
action_taken: Not applicable; statistical measurement, not an intervention.
outcome_evidence: Population-level: 2023 set a record at 5.5 million applications, the third straight year above 5 million.
source_limitations: Population dataset with no firm-level outcome; cannot support a single-company diagnosis. Applications are an entry signal, not survival or success; many applications never become employer businesses. Annual totals are rounded and revised over time. Distinct from the slice-1 BLS Business Employment Dynamics record: this is Census BFS formation/entry data, not BLS establishment births/deaths. Census pages returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; figures confirmed verbatim in census.gov and corroborating primary/secondary snippets (Census, EIG, SBA).
directly_stated: Approximately 5.3 million applications in 2022 and 5.4 million in 2021
Third consecutive year above 5 million applications
Seasonally adjusted monthly applications about 464,838 (Nov 2023) and 472,961 (Sep 2023)
Applications measured via EIN; formations measured via first payroll-tax liability
inferred: Sustained record formation indicates a healthy U.S. business-entry environment as a base rate
High application counts say nothing about which firms will survive or struggle
why_useful_for_opsiq: Authoritative U.S. business-formation base rate, distinct from the slice-1 BLS record. Useful for stable-healthy base-rate calibration (outcome 12) and for teaching OpsIQ that population entry-flow data does not license a firm-level diagnosis.
